title: Build apartments and commercial buildings to the building code (NCC Volume One)
what: Ensure building work on Class 2 to 9 buildings complies with the Building Act 2016 and all applicable provisions of the National Construction Code (Volume One, with the Tasmanian variations). The edition in force is NCC 2022 until 30 April 2027 and the latest edition from 1 May 2027, under the Building Amendment Act 2026. Its schedule in NCC 2025 varies 159 national provisions, 136 of them in special use buildings (Section I).

sources.title: Building Act 2016 (Tas)
sources.quote: 11. All work must comply with Act and National Construction Code (1) A person performing building work, plumbing work or demolition work must ensure that the work complies with – (a) this Act; and (b) all of the applicable provisions of the National Construction Code, unless otherwise authorised under this Act.

sources.title: Building Act 2016 (Tas)
sources.quote: National Construction Code means – (a) until 30 April 2027 – the edition of the National Construction Code published by the Australian Building Codes Board entitled NCC 2022, and as last amended by NCC 2022 Amendment 2 on 29 July 2025; and (b) on and from 1 May 2027 – the latest edition of that code published by the Australian Building Codes Board, including as amended, from time to time.

sources.title: Building Act 2016 (Tas)
sources.locator: s 11(4), words naming the body (found 27 Nov 2026) (current)
sources.quote: (4) A building surveyor, as far as is reasonably practicable, is to ensure that all building work and demolition work, in respect of which he or she is engaged as a building surveyor, is performed in accordance with this Act.

triggers.note: when carrying out building work on a Class 2 to 9 building (apartments, hotels, offices, shops, factories, warehouses, car parks, public buildings)

reach.note: Volume One covers Class 2 to 9 buildings. Builders in other classes (building trades) doing such work are bound too; only the main builders are coded here.

confidence_note: The law's own words require building or plumbing work to comply with the code. Drafted on 27 November 2026 for the NCC work (docs/plan_ncc_ingestion.md, phase N3); the variation counts are from the NCC 2025 dataset.

assessment.summary: Work must meet the National Construction Code (Volume One) as Tasmania applies it. The code sets minimum safety, health, amenity, accessibility and energy standards, whose benefits are not weighed here; meeting and certifying them adds to the cost of every project.

marks.reason: Designing, documenting and certifying each project against the code adds cost, and the state's own variations add to it for builders who work in several states.

assessment.confidence_note: Marked to agree with the NCC adoption records (burden -1); the Productivity Commission finds several code changes were adopted although their impact analyses showed a net cost. No evaluation of the requirement itself was found.
